question: Should maintainers revive the open cross-repository repair, replace it with a narrow same-repo repair, or close that candidate before continuing?
rationale: The code fix shape is clear, but the only open linked implementation is outside the target repository, conflicting, and not maintainer-editable, so automation should not open another competing fix without maintainer direction.

options.title: Replace With Narrow Same-Repo Repair
options.body: Open or adopt a clean same-repo fix that applies the shared-schema move on current main and credits the prior repair work.

options.title: Ask Fork Author To Rebase
options.body: Keep the issue linked to the open fork PR and ask its author to rebase and enable maintainer edits before review can continue.

options.title: Defer Without New Work
options.body: Leave the issue open until the fork PR is closed or becomes landable, accepting that the docs/schema mismatch remains in current main and the latest release.

recommendation.title: Replace With Narrow Same-Repo Repair
recommendation.body: Open or adopt a clean same-repo fix that applies the shared-schema move on current main and credits the prior repair work.
